review_scope.method: 34 original JPEGs individually viewed at original resolution, in increasing capture-frame order. Five consecutive screenshots 1684-1688 cover the logged brief effort. Other samples are sparse; only selected instants were visually assessed.

ordinary_encounter_facts.visible_weapon: M1911 only; common runner requested fields are defaults for other modes, not encounter weapon acquisition.
ordinary_encounter_facts.input_limit: Simulated production-controller WASD/LMB edges with target-selected projected torso cursor. This actual input log contains no R, modifier, interaction or sprint edges. Press count is not a committed-shot count.
ordinary_encounter_facts.setup_limit: Encounter branch leaves normal spawning/scoring/health/ammo authoritative. No encounter grants, teleports, forced damage, forced falls or health restores. Scripted repeating movement and automatic target/cursor selection are not native play.

effort.interpretation: A real bounded physical effort stopped early; a later genuine recovery occurred. This capture does not establish that the effort caused the eventual clearance.

intervening_corpse_disappearance.inference: The spatially corresponding blue corpse disappears before GetUp. Its approximately 28-second observed dead lifespan is consistent with ordinary corpse retirement. The effort log blocker name is not directly mapped to this observation ID, so exact blocker identity/causality is not asserted.

findings: The blue workwear, white lab coat and taupe shirt/brown-trouser variants remain distinguishable in ordinary arena bodies; several approaching live figures are readable. This does not visually identify every observed actor.

Pursuit around benches, depleted pistol ammunition, blood, corpses, scoring and a round transition appear in the selected originals. Early lethal impacts themselves were not sampled; their exact moments are not a pixel-review claim.

Staff contact stumble/fall progresses from upright-over-corpse to a physical floor pose. The pair remains together through the brief effort. Small effort travel is telemetry evidence; moving-camera/upper-edge images do not resolve centimetre-scale efficacy.

The nearby corpse disappears before recovery. Staff then extends into the authored prone start, presses through its arms, brings a knee/foot under the body and rises. Final upright balance is partly cropped, while subsequent pursuit is fully visible.
No obvious exploding mesh, missing body/material silhouette or large position jump appears in these selected frames. Broad continuous seam/foot-slide/animation smoothness approval is not established.

The character waits about 14.6 seconds from logged fall to get-up start, including a stopped effort and 18 blocked checks. This is evidence of eventual recovery after local occupancy changes, not a guarantee that every blocked body escapes quickly.
limits: Static chronological samples, not continuous video; actor identity comes from telemetry/position/garment correlation, not visible ID labels.
Frame world_seconds, actor elapsed seconds and log UTC/frame counter are retained as separate clocks. No fabricated time offset or exact interpolation.
Source transport has 109.717333 seconds of master-output WAV; it was not listened to. Screenshot cadence/recording overhead is not a performance result.
Three engine assertions cover encounter startup and capture transport, not a comprehensive numerical combat/recovery test suite.
Player HP falls to 81 and later returns to 100 through the normal system; HealthRestores remains zero. Infected health remains 100.8 through the observed fall/recovery.
One last living infected remains and the M1911 is empty in the late sample. The second wave is not completed.
